title: RoleChange
description: The outcome of evaluating a role change, derived from identity_application::administration::RoleChange. This is one of only two things in identity-application with a REAL BODY rather than a trait signature: RoleChangeRequest::evaluate is a pure function, and it exists here rather than in identity-domain because the rule needs a COUNT OF ADMINISTRATORS — a fact about the current state of the store, not a property of a single user.
x-serde-status: the type and the rule behind it are IMPLEMENTED; the command that would apply the outcome, ChangeUserRoleCommand, has no body
x-serde-note: Internally tagged: #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "outcome")]. The discriminator is the field 'outcome', NOT a key in an externally-tagged union, because no client can switch on an externally-tagged enum without parsing the key first.

oneOf.title: Permitted
oneOf.description: The change is permitted and should be applied. Note what this does NOT mean: it means the RULE did not refuse. It does not mean the change has been applied — a console must not report success before the command has committed.

oneOf.title: LastAdministrator
oneOf.description: Refused: this would leave the platform with no active administrator. Fires only when the change would REMOVE an active administrator — a demotion, or a change of role away from administrator, on a target whose status is active — and the count is at or below one. A suspended administrator is not counted, which is precisely why RoleChangeRequest.target_status is an input rather than something the function re-reads.

user_id.description: The user who would have been demoted. Named so an operator reading the refusal knows exactly whose demotion was refused.

oneOf.title: SelfChange
oneOf.description: Refused: a user cannot change their own role. Self-promotion is the privilege-escalation primitive; the only way to grant a role is for ANOTHER administrator to grant it. Checked FIRST, before the last-administrator rule, so a lone administrator demoting themselves gets the honest reason rather than the misleading one.

oneOf.title: NotPermitted
oneOf.description: Refused: the actor's role may not assign the target role. Checked BEFORE the administrator count is consulted, so a support actor demoting the last administrator gets the authorization refusal — the last-administrator reason would be misleading for a problem that is really 'you may not do this at all'. The check is on the ACTOR, not the direction of the change: a member promoting someone to administrator is refused too, and so is the Service role the Jobs Worker holds.

role.description: Which role was refused — the role being ASSIGNED, not the actor's role.

x-evaluation-order.why-the-order-is-load-bearing: identity_application::administration::tests::self_change_is_reported_before_the_last_administrator_rule asserts a lone administrator demoting themselves gets SelfChange, not LastAdministrator. Both apply; the self-change reason is the more useful one.

x-concurrency-requirement.rule: the active_administrator_count passed into the rule must be computed INSIDE THE SAME TRANSACTION that applies the change
x-concurrency-requirement.why: two simultaneous demotions must not both see two administrators. The count and the change belong in one transaction, and Phase 6's exit condition requires the test to actually race them.
x-concurrency-requirement.the-console-does-not-pre-empt-this: the operator console does NOT disable the control client-side. A client-side 'you cannot demote the last administrator' check is a check the client can be wrong about, and a disabled control is a control that explains nothing. The console shows the server's refusal when it arrives.

x-error-shape: The command itself returns ApplicationResult<PlatformRole> — a PlatformRole on success, an error on refusal. RoleChange is what the pure rule returns internally; whether a refusal reaches the client as a 403 envelope or as this body is a Phase 6 decision, and this contract does not claim it is settled. The 403 envelope is the documented status mapping for 'forbidden'.
